summary: Constructor for the minimal SMTP wrapper. Stores the connection target (host + port) on the instance fields. No socket is opened — that happens in TIdSMTPMin.Connect on first use. The caller becomes the owner of the constructed instance; Delphi's manual memory management means an explicit Free is required (in .NET this maps to IDisposable / using; in Java to try-with-resources via AutoCloseable).

inputs.name: AHost
inputs.semantic: DNS name or IP of the SMTP server. Stored verbatim; no validation or trim.

inputs.name: APort
inputs.semantic: TCP port. Caller is responsible for using a standard port (25, 465, 587) or a custom one; no range check.

invariants.claim: FHost is set to the AHost parameter; FPort is set to the APort parameter; no other instance state is mutated.
The base-class constructor (inherited Create) is called before any field assignment, so TIdBaseComponent invariants hold on completion.

object_lifetimes.subject: Self (return value)
object_lifetimes.policy: Caller owns the returned instance and MUST call Free / Destroy. In .NET this maps to IDisposable + Dispose pattern; in Java to AutoCloseable + try-with-resources.

interface_implementations.obligation: By virtue of inheriting from TIdBaseComponent the constructed instance participates in the Indy component lifecycle (Active / Inactive states, hooks for sub-component composition). The constructor itself does not enforce additional contracts beyond the base-class call.

edge_cases.description: AHost is empty string. No validation; FHost is set to '' and the failure surfaces later during Connect.
edge_cases.behavior: Constructor completes normally; the bad-host symptom appears at Connect time as a socket resolution failure.

edge_cases.description: APort is non-positive or above 65535. No range check; the value flows into the eventual socket-connect call where the OS rejects it.
edge_cases.behavior: Constructor completes normally; failure deferred to Connect.

open_questions.question: Should AHost be trimmed of leading / trailing whitespace before storage, or is the caller responsible? The source does not normalise.
